[[NIT Season Tip-Off]] champions |tourney = [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = [[2018 UMBC vs. Virginia men's basketball game|First Round]] }} {{2017–18 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Virginia]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by head coach [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] in his ninth year, and played their home games at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. In a year with low expectations from the press, the Cavaliers began unranked but ascended all the way to the No. 1 ranking in the AP Poll for the first time since [[1982–83 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|December 1982]].{{cite news|url=http://wtvr.com/2018/02/12/virginia-number-1/|title=Virginia ranked #1 in new AP college basketball poll|last1=Casadonte|first1=Lane|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018|publisher=[[WTVR-TV]]|last2=Robertson|first2=Sean|location=[[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond, VA]]}}{{efn|The Cavaliers also became the first team in the AP Poll era, dating to the 1948–49 season, to rise to #1 despite losing a game in the prior week (at home in overtime to [[2017–18 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]]). Virginia's rise was aided by the previous #1 and #3 teams, respectively [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] and [[2017–18 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], also losing at home.}} The team then held on to that ranking through the end of the regular season and became the first ACC team to win 17 conference games. The Cavaliers won the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] by handily defeating Louisville 75–58, Clemson 64–58, and North Carolina 71–63 in the championship game. In the process the team broke the school's single-season win record, which had twice been tied by Bennett-led teams in the past five years. ACC Sixth Man of the Year [[De'Andre Hunter]] broke his wrist in the ACC Tournament victory, and was announced to be out for the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] two days before it began.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/13/virginia-deandre-hunter-miss-ncaa-tournament-broken-wrist|title=Virginia's De'Andre Hunter Will Miss NCAA Tournament Due to Broken Wrist|last=Rollins|first=Khadrice|date=March 13, 2018|website=www.si.com|publisher=Sports Illustrated|access-date=March 18, 2018}} UVA entered as the No. 1 overall seed, placed in the South regional, but suffered [[2018 UMBC vs. Virginia men's basketball game|an upset]] in the first round to [[2017–18 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC]] and became the first No. 1 seed to lose to a No. 16 seed since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/121935/umbc-does-the-unthinkable-becoming-the-first-16-seed-to-beat-a-no-1-seed|title=UMBC does the unthinkable, becoming the first Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|No. 2 seed Cincinnati]] and [[2017–18 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|No. 3 seed Tennessee]], led to the South Region becoming the first ever to not advance any of its top four seeds to the Sweet Sixteen.[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2765368-fsus-leonard-hamilton-almost-like-a-revolution-with-march-madness-upsets Leonard Hamilton: Upsets Almost Like a Revolution], accessed March 19, 2018 Nevertheless, for taking an unranked team to finish four games above pre-season AP No. 1 ranked [[2017–18 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] and winning the ACC Tournament over [[2017–18 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], Bennett was awarded his third [[Henry Iba Award]] for the nation's top coach They defeated [[2016–17 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] in the second round of the [[2017 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] to advance to the quarterfinals where they lost to [[2016–17 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]].
